question: Your team's project CLAUDE.md has grown to include a long step-by-step procedure for generating database migration scripts, which developers use only a few times per month. The same file also holds the team's naming conventions and error-handling standards, which apply to every code change. Developers report that the migration procedure adds clutter to every Claude Code session. How should you restructure this configuration?

options.text: Move both the migration procedure and the coding standards into skills, so that the project CLAUDE.md loads nothing until a developer invokes a skill.
options.reason: Universal standards belong in the always-loaded CLAUDE.md; as on-demand skills they would apply only when a developer remembers to invoke them.

options.text: Keep the migration procedure in the project CLAUDE.md, and move the naming and error-handling standards into a skill that developers invoke before each change.
options.reason: This reverses the guidance: the occasional workflow stays always loaded, and the universal standards become on-demand and easy to skip.

options.text: Move the migration procedure into each developer's user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, so that it loads only for the developers who generate migrations.
options.reason: User-level CLAUDE.md is not shared via version control and is still always loaded in every session, so it neither shares the workflow nor makes it on-demand.

options.text: Move the migration procedure into a skill in .claude/skills/ for on-demand invocation, and keep the naming and error-handling standards in the project CLAUDE.md.
options.reason: Skills suit task-specific workflows invoked on demand, while CLAUDE.md is always loaded and suits universal standards that apply to every change.
